text:
cs_jordan: customer Acme reporting a sudden spike of 401s this morning after operator upgrade. They pasted a curl and response:

cs_jordan: ```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" https://acme.api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{
  "error": { "type": "invalid_api_key", "message": "The provided API key is not valid." }
}
```

cs_jordan: Any quick ideas? customer says nothing changed on their side except the infra operator got bumped to v1.2.0

eng_amy: Are they on Private or Dedicated? Also can you grab the request-id from our infra logs for that timestamp?

cs_jordan: Private (on-prem). request-id from our side: req_20260317_1402_az12. Secret name they've been using: `acme-api-key` in namespace `acme-prod`.

leo_sre: pulling logs now... seeing repeated 401s for that request-id. Can you run and paste (obfuscate) the k8s secret data value?

cs_jordan: pasted base64 snippet (trimmed): `U0dWc2J...==`

eng_amy: that base64 decodes to *another* base64 blob. suspicious — looks like the operator double-encoded the value when seeding the secret. Quick check you can run locally on their cluster:

eng_amy: ```bash
# inspect raw value then decode twice to verify
kubectl get secret acme-api-key -n acme-prod -o jsonpath='{.data.key}' | base64 --decode | base64 --decode -w0
```

eng_amy: if the output is their human-readable API key (starts with `ri_`) then it's double-encoded. To fix safely:

eng_amy: ```bash
# safer step-by-step
DECODED=$(kubectl get secret acme-api-key -n acme-prod -o jsonpath='{.data.key}' | base64 --decode)
# DECODED now contains the single-encoded bytes; make sure it begins with ri_ when decoded again
echo -n "$DECODED" | base64 --decode -w0  # verify human-readable key
# patch secret with single-base64 encoding of the actual key
CORRECT_B64=$(echo -n "$(echo -n $DECODED | base64 --decode -w0)" | base64 -w0)
kubectl patch secret acme-api-key -n acme-prod --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/key","value":"'$CORRECT_B64'"}]'
# then rollout restart the deployment/service that reads it
kubectl rollout restart deployment acme-api-frontend -n acme-prod
```

leo_sre: ran the decode check in their cluster — confirmed the double-base64 pattern and after patching and restarting the frontend, traffic for that request-id returned 200s.

deploy-bot: Deployment acme-api-frontend restarted by leo_sre (rolling restart) :rocket:

eng_amy: root cause: operator v1.2.0 introduced a double-base64 when writing secret.data.key for external API keys (GH#482). PR 483 fixes it; recommend rolling to operator v1.2.5. We'll open a patch release and notify on-prem customers running 1.2.0/1.2.1.

cs_jordan: customer confirmed verification, 200s coming back now. I'll send final note and close the ticket. :white_check_mark:

eng_amy: I'll file a short postmortem and add a provisioning checklist item to decode/verify secret values after operator upgrades. Also adding an automated unit check in the operator repo to prevent regressions.
